 Mumbai: Threat mail received at BMC office; nothing suspicious found during check
 ANI | 
 Updated: Oct 23, 2026 14:07 IST 
 ANI News
 Join our Whatsapp channel 
 Mumbai (Maharashtra) [India], October 23 (ANI): A threat email was received at the Brihanmumbai Municipal Corporation (BMC) office, following which a check was conducted and nothing suspicious was found, Mumbai Police said.
The BMC, the civic body responsible for municipal administration and the provision of essential civic services in Mumbai , received the threat email, prompting security checks at its office.
According to Mumbai Police, the checking process was carried out after the email was received, but no suspicious object or material was found during the inspection.
 An almost same incident of threat mail occured on March 20, the Mumbai Press Club received a threatening email claiming that several small bombs filled with poisonous gas had been planted inside the building and would explode at 1 pm, an official said.
According to initial information, the email was allegedly sent by an individual identifying themselves as Neeraja Ajmal Khan. The sender claimed that as many as 42 "poison gas" devices had been installed inside the Press Club building.
The mail stated that, "We, the Muslims of Coimbatore, have learned a harsh truth: Udhayanidhi's cunning family used us as a mere vote bank and punished us in the name of protecting us. All our leaders who supported DMK in the last election have now been arrested under 'UAPA' by the same Udhayanidhi whom we had supported.
When we tried to expose them, Tamil Nadu media outlets blocked us. So, we came to your state, but you also disappointed us."The mail also claimed that the alleged devices were intended only for property damage and urged that the building be evacuated. (ANI)
